notes:
### Dorcel Buffering

- Dorcel playback now uses a 35-second InputStream Adaptive live delay to keep playback farther away from the unstable live edge and better absorb the recurring 20–25-second source windows identified in the HAR/browser comparison.
- The goal is to shorten or eliminate the periodic still-image stalls instead of reacting to every source window with a restart.

### Source-Aware Diagnostics

- Dorcel manifest diagnostics now parse EXT-X-TARGETDURATION and EXTINF segment durations and log target duration, maximum segment duration, playlist window and unchanged-manifest age.
- Added SOURCE_WINDOW classification for stalls that occur during known long Dorcel HLS segment/publication windows instead of incorrectly treating them as Kodi-only stalls.

### Recovery

- An unchanged manifest is no longer treated as broken after only two short probes. Stale recovery now waits for a duration derived from the manifest, with a minimum of 30 seconds and additional safety margin beyond the observed target/segment duration.
- A media-sequence reset by itself no longer forces a fresh Dorcel session because the website player was observed recovering from these resets on the same signed session.
- Confirmed HTTP/manifest failures remain eligible for immediate recovery.

### Important

- Existing stall IDs, Wi-Fi diagnostics, hourly handoff measurements, Auto Channels Check, Site/IPTV behavior, One Channel, automatic log saving, Save Log Only, Shutdown/Sleep, Check Lock and AlarmClock/watchdog remain otherwise unchanged.
